message.content:
In this repository, memos (notes) carry derived metadata computed from their content rather than set directly by the user - things like a title/preview extracted from content, word count, tags parsed from content, etc, used for lists/previews.

Find:
1. Where this derived metadata is computed (exact file path and function/method name)
2. What operations/triggers cause it to be recomputed (e.g., on save, on create, via a hook, a background job, a database trigger, etc.)
3. What specific properties are extracted/computed (e.g., title, snippet, word count, tags, links, etc.)

Search the codebase thoroughly - look for models/entities named "Memo" or "Note", and look for functions with names like "extractMetadata", "computeMetadata", "parseContent", "beforeSave", "preSave" hooks, etc.

Report back with exact file paths and line numbers, and code snippets showing the computation logic and where it's invoked.

- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

- review: Review a GitHub pull request; for your working diff use /code-review
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

content.text:
I now have a complete picture. Here's the report.

## Summary

This is the **memos** Go backend (github.com/usememos/memos). Derived memo metadata is computed by a markdown-parsing service and stored in a protobuf `Payload` column on the memo row.

### 1. Where it's computed

**Core extraction logic:** `/bench/repo/internal/markdown/markdown.go`, in the `service` struct (implements the `markdown.Service` interface, built on `goldmark`):

- `ExtractAll(content []byte) (*ExtractedData, error)` — lines 356-422. Single-pass AST walk that extracts tags, mentions, and properties together (the "efficient" combined extractor).
- `ExtractTags` — lines 143-170 (standalone `#tag` extraction).
- `ExtractProperties` — lines 193-241 (standalone boolean-property extraction).
- `GenerateSnippet(content []byte, maxLength int) (string, error)` — lines 264-346 (plain-text preview/snippet generation, truncated at word boundary).

**Invocation wrapper (the "computeMetadata" entry point):** `/bench/repo/server/runner/memopayload/runner.go`:
```go
func RebuildMemoPayload(_ context.Context, memo *store.Memo, markdownService markdown.Service) error {
	if memo.Payload == nil {
		memo.Payload = &storepb.MemoPayload{}
	}
	data, err := markdownService.ExtractAll([]byte(memo.Content))
	if err != nil {
		return errors.Wrap(err, "failed to extract markdown metadata")
	}
	memo.Payload.Tags = data.Tags
	memo.Payload.Property = data.Property
	return nil
}
```
(lines 74-88)

### 2. What triggers recomputation

- **On memo create** — `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:108`, inside `CreateMemo`: `memopayload.RebuildMemoPayload(ctx, create, s.MarkdownService)` is called before `s.Store.CreateMemo(...)`.
- **On memo update, only when content changes** — `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:447`, inside `UpdateMemo`, gated on `path == "content"` from the update mask: content is reassigned, then `RebuildMemoPayload` is called again before persisting.
- **Bulk/backfill batch job** — `/bench/repo/server/runner/memopayload/runner.go`, `Runner.RunOnce` (lines 27-72): paginates through all memos (`ListMemos`, batch size 100) and calls `RebuildMemoPayload` + `Store.UpdateMemo` for each. However, unlike the `s3presign` runner, this one is **not wired into `startBackgroundRunners`** in `/bench/repo/server/server.go` (only `s3presign.NewRunner` is started there, lines 153-174) — it appears to be a standalone/migration-style utility, not currently invoked automatically at server startup or on a schedule.
- **Snippet is NOT stored** — it's computed on-demand at read/serialization time, not persisted as part of the payload:
  - `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service_webhooks.go:83-89` — `getMemoContentSnippet` calls `MarkdownService.GenerateSnippet([]byte(content), 64)`.
  - Called from `memo_service_converter.go:76` (converting a memo to its API response) and `memo_relation_service.go:154/162` (related-memo snippets), and `user_service_notifications.go:318-327` (notification snippets).
- **Mentions** are extracted via the same `ExtractAll` call but used transiently for @mention notification dispatch (`/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_mention_helpers.go:26-38`, `resolveMentionTargets`) — not persisted to the payload (only `Tags` and `Property` are saved in `RebuildMemoPayload`).

### 3. What properties are extracted

Defined in `/bench/repo/proto/store/memo.proto` (lines 7-29), populated by `ExtractAll`/`ExtractProperties` in markdown.go:

- **Tags** (`repeated string tags`) — all `#tag` occurrences in content, deduped, case-preserved, skipping tags inside links/images.
- **Property.title** — text of the first H1 heading, if it's the first block-level element in the document (`extractHeadingText`, markdown.go:172-179, 384-389).
- **Property.has_link** — set if any markdown link node is present.
- **Property.has_code** — set if any code block, fenced code block, or inline code span is present.
- **Property.has_task_list** — set if any GFM task checkbox is present.
- **Property.has_incomplete_tasks** — set if any task checkbox is unchecked.
- **Snippet** (not stored, computed on read) — plain-text preview, code blocks stripped, truncated to `maxLength` (64 chars for API responses) at a word boundary with a `...` suffix.
- **Mentions** (transient, not persisted) — lowercased `@username` mentions, used only to resolve notification targets.
- **Location** (`Property.Location`: placeholder/lat/lng) exists in the same payload message but is user-supplied via the request (`memo_service.go:111-113`), not derived from content.

No word-count field exists in this codebase.
